## Findings
- claim-1: The paper’s formal conjecture is that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are inclusion-minimal; “minimal” means no proper subset generates. [source-6@L14-L16|claim=ordinary-document] [source-6@L41-L44|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The authors report only finite computational verification, for bigrassmannians with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: The stronger suspected statement is \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), and the source says a proof had eluded the authors. [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-4: A universal common-cardinality assertion over \(\mathbb Z\) is false. Let \(R=\mathbb Z[x]\) and \(I=(2x,3x)=(x)\). Both \(\{x\}\) and \(\{2x,3x\}\) are homogeneous generating sets; the latter is inclusion-minimal since \(x\notin(2x)\) and \(x\notin(3x)\). Their cardinalities are \(1\) and \(2\).
- claim-5: Let \(R=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}R_d\) with \(R_0=\mathbb Z\), \(R_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}R_d\), and let \(M\) be a bounded-below, finitely generated graded \(R\)-module. Put \(Q=M/R_+M\). Homogeneous generating sets of \(M\) are inclusion-minimal exactly when their images are inclusion-minimal homogeneous \(\mathbb Z\)-generating sets of \(Q\): if the images generate \(Q\), then \(M=N+R_+M\), where \(N\) is generated by the lifts; the bounded-below graded Nakayama argument gives \(M=N\).
- claim-6: Under these hypotheses, all inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets of \(M\) have a common cardinality if and only if every nonzero graded abelian group \(Q_d\) is finite \(p_d\)-primary for some prime \(p_d\) (the prime may depend on \(d\)). In that case the common cardinality is \(\sum_d\dim_{\mathbb F_{p_d}}(Q_d/p_dQ_d)\). Sufficiency follows from Nakayama over the local ring \(\mathbb Z/p_d^{e_d}\). Conversely, a free summand yields the irredundant alternatives \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\) in \(\mathbb Z\); two distinct primary parts yield respectively an irredundant union of primary generators and an irredundant CRT-aligned generating set, of different sizes.
- claim-7: Consequently, freeness of \(M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(\mathbb Z\), even if established, does not by itself imply common cardinality for arbitrary inclusion-minimal generating sets: \(\mathbb Z\) is free but has the irredundant generating sets \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\).
## Strategy
- The unrestricted common-cardinality assertion is refuted by claim-4.
- Under \(R_0=\mathbb Z\), nonnegative grading, and bounded-below finitely generated graded \(M\), reduce homogeneous minimal generating families of \(M\) to indexed homogeneous irredundant \(\mathbb Z\)-generating families of
  \[
  Q=M/R_+M
  \]
  via graded Nakayama.
- Degreewise, the exact proposed criterion is: all such families have one cardinality iff every nonzero \(Q_d\) is finite \(p_d\)-primary for one prime \(p_d\). Then the cardinality is
  \[
  \sum_d\dim_{\mathbb F_{p_d}}(Q_d/p_dQ_d).
  \]
  A free summand or two distinct primary components in one degree produces irredundant families of different sizes.
- For the two specified Theorem 5.4 sets, the weaker conditional route is sufficient: if \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) and each displayed set has \(N\) elements, each is inclusion-minimal. This does not imply common cardinality for arbitrary irredundant sets.

## Gaps
- The immutable statement and hypotheses of “accepted claim 9” are absent.
- No supplied evidence identifies the cardinalities of the two Theorem 5.4 sets or computes the graded abelian group \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\).
- Claims 5–6 require a complete proof, including the indexed-family formulation, graded Nakayama step, and explicit CRT/free-summand counterfamilies.
- Thus the source-specific conjecture for \(J_v\) remains unresolved; claim-2 supplies only finite computational evidence.

## Next
- Obtain the exact claim-9 text and the source formulas/cardinalities for both candidate sets.
- Prove the reduction \(M\leftrightarrow Q\) using a least-degree argument, then prove the finite-abelian-group criterion degree by degree.
- Establish the structure, or at least the rank and torsion decomposition, of \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), and compare it with both candidate cardinalities.
- Submit the completed conditional theorem and any \(J_v\)-specific computation for independent review.
